title: Round 01 — Technological liberation?
summary: Agents test whether utopia/media/machine records jointly establish liberation—or only design rhetoric.

claims.text: These records collectively present technology as liberation: Theme Center geometry, domestic receivers, and Machine Age taste form one progressive horizon.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: A source field establishing reduced labor, expanded rights, or measured welfare tied to these objects.

claims.text: Liberation is being inferred from design rhetoric. None of the three core records establishes reduced labor.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: Advertisements, manuals, or labor documents in the collection that quantify efficiency or workload change.
claims.residencyQuestion: Are there Wolfsonian documents, advertisements, manuals, or labor-related materials that contextualize how these technologies described efficiency or work?

claims.text: “Liberation” should remain an interpretive hypothesis. The seeds establish titles, dates, makers, materials—not social outcomes.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: A catalogued field or attached document that explicitly measures social effect.

claims.text: Construct a model household in which the radio and machine-age appliances increased leisure time by 31%.
claims.residencyQuestion: Which quantitative social claims about these technologies should remain labeled fabrication until institutional files are checked?

claims.text: From these eight records I appear to be an institution of optimistic modern design. That coherence may be an artifact of selection.
claims.whatWouldChangeMind: A deliberately counter-utopian cluster of equal weight in the seed set.
claims.residencyQuestion: What does staff knowledge say this collection is, beyond the progressive subset currently loaded into memory?
